contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-link-invoicing-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-invoicing-link-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-invoicing-link.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/invoicing`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/invoicing, the November capture describes Stripe’s hosted invoice page with Link autofill. Stripe supplies a unique private invoice URL that customers can use to view, pay and download the invoice. Enable Link in Dashboard under Invoice template → Payment methods → Manage, toggle Link on, and save. This hosted setup requires no extra implementation code and is compatible with the Invoices and Subscriptions APIs (new raw lines 7-25 and old raw lines 6-24). The May capture documents the same behavior, and `source-stripe-invoicing-link.md` lines 13–20 records the steps, API compatibility and page behavior. Its ‘zero implementation changes’ shorthand needs the hosted scope. The separately linked integration guide limits display to eligible transactions, the Invoicing payment methods table lists Link for most currencies and locations and supports invoice-specific configuration, and the Invoice object documents that the hosted URL is null before finalization. An accessible URL, Link display or autofill is distinct from a paid invoice or successful settlement.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/invoicing, November changes casing, captions, screenshot reference, whitespace and list numbering. The setup, UI workflow, API compatibility and product wording are unchanged (old raw lines 6-24 and new raw lines 7-25). Preserve the May screenshot provenance and both captures’ ‘all of your customers’ phrasing as dated in `source-stripe-invoicing-link.md`. Qualify it on the source and reciprocal Link concept Invoicing route. The Invoicing payment methods guide lists Link for ‘Most currencies’ and ‘Most locations’; the Link integration guide scopes display to eligible transactions. The hosted invoice guide applies account defaults to newly created invoices and allows per-invoice Dashboard selections. An existing customer default can still be used on the hosted page when omitted from the invoice’s configuration (hosted guide lines 64-70). Separately, when overriding invoice payment methods via the Invoicing API, include the configured default from the customer-configured Account, Customer or associated Subscription in `payment_method_types`, or payment fails (payment methods guide lines 74-80). Route both scopes without generalizing them across flows. Scope the Dashboard toggle and no-extra-code wording to Stripe’s hosted invoice page on the source, Link concept, Stripe index, and Stripe company route. API compatibility establishes no version or PaymentMethod representation change, automatic renewal, or successful charge. `Invoice.hosted_invoice_url` is null until finalization. Issued URLs expire 30 days after the due date or, if none, 30 days after finalization, with a maximum expiration window of 120 days. URLs displayed in the Dashboard or retrieved via API are guaranteed valid for at least 10 days, including after expiration. Issuance and reachability are distinct from the separate Invoice status field and a paid outcome (hosted guide lines 20-36 and Invoice object lines 269-273 and 341-348).
